Subject: Post-call: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - next steps

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the next steps we agreed on for integration into Acme Health's staging environment: 

- Goal: Private connectivity for Redwood API so traffic never traverses the public internet (VPC endpoints + IP allowlist + enforced mTLS).
- Requirements you listed: egress restrictions to partner APIs, internal DNS resolution for redwood-internal endpoints, and SOC2-friendly audit logs.
- Technical asks for next email: a) VPC architecture (are you using AWS VPC with Transit Gateway?), b) whether you prefer interface or gateway endpoints, c) current IP ranges to add to allowlist, and d) whether your egress goes through NAT or a firewall appliance.

Action items we agreed: 
1) Sophie to share a basic network topology diagram + the egress/NAT details (by EOD Friday).
2) Redwood to send a short implementation guide for VPC endpoints, IP allowlist, and mTLS requirements (we'll include SDK auth patterns and sample routing policy).
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync next week to walk through the plan.

I attached our VPC integration guide that covers interface vs gateway endpoints, DNS considerations, and a sample mTLS configuration. If you can also include a list of CIDR blocks we should expect, we can prepare the allowlist and provide a canary rollout plan for staging.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- We're on AWS, using multiple VPCs connected via Transit Gateway. Our egress to the internet goes through a centralized NAT/egress firewall in the shared services account.
- For private connectivity we'd prefer interface endpoints if possible, but we need guidance on DNS override and mTLS certificates.
- Initial staging CIDRs: 10.12.0.0/16 and 10.13.0.0/16. We can expose a small set of static egress IPs from the firewall team.

I'll attach a high-level topology diagram and confirm the exact public egress IPs by tomorrow. Also please include the SDK/auth sample you mentioned — our app team will want examples for token exchange and refresh.

Cheers,
Sophie
Senior Product Manager — Integrations
Acme Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 18:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - next steps

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the details. A few notes from the infra side and what we can provide out-of-the-box: 

1) Endpoints & DNS
- We support interface endpoints with private DNS override; we'll provide a CNAME target you can add to your private hosted zone to resolve api.redwood-internal.example -> our endpoint IPs.

2) IP allowlist / egress
- CIDRs 10.12.0.0/16 and 10.13.0.0/16 are fine for staging; however, allowlisting is done at the public egress. If you can provide the firewall's outbound static IPs we will add those to our access control list API.

3) mTLS & auth
- mTLS is optional but supported. For the most secure setup we recommend mTLS between your egress gateway and our VPC endpoint. We'll accept client certs signed by your PKI; we also support ACME/Let's Encrypt for short-lived certs.
- For SDK auth, our recommended pattern for server-to-server is short-lived JWTs exchanged via our OAuth token endpoint. We'll send sample code for Node/Python.

4) Routing & structured output/tool calling
- If you plan to use tool calling or external connectors that call back out to external APIs, route those through your approved egress so audit logs capture downstream calls.

I've attached a short implementation checklist and a sample mTLS config. Happy to walk through these in the tech sync.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
